name: form-validation
description: Create a form with comprehensive validation

promptLevels.novice: check if form fields are valid
promptLevels.beginner: make a form validator that checks if username and email are filled out correctly
promptLevels.intermediate: create a FormValidator class that takes form data and validation rules, then returns which fields have errors
promptLevels.advanced: write a FormValidator class that accepts form data (object) and validation rules (object defining requirements per field), validates each field, and returns an errors object listing all validation failures
promptLevels.expert: Write a FormValidator class that validates form data against configurable rules. The class should: 1) Accept form data as an object (e.g., {username: 'john', email: 'john@example.com'}). 2) Accept validation rules as an object where each key corresponds to a form field and contains validation requirements. Rules should support: required (boolean), minLength (number), maxLength (number), pattern (regex), and custom validator functions. 3) Have a validate() method that checks all fields against their rules and returns an errors object. The errors object should have keys for each invalid field with values being error message strings or arrays of messages. 4) Return an empty errors object {} if all validations pass. Example rule: {username: {required: true, minLength: 3}, email: {required: true, pattern: /^[^@]+@[^@]+$/}}. The validator should generate appropriate error messages for each failed rule. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with generics for form data type. Define interfaces: ValidationRule (with optional properties for required, minLength, maxLength, pattern, custom), ValidationRules<T> (mapping field names to rules), ValidationErrors (mapping field names to string or string[]). The validate() method should return ValidationErrors. Export the class and interfaces.
languageInstructions.javascript: Create a FormValidator class with constructor accepting formData and rules objects. Implement validation logic that checks each rule type and builds error messages. Use Object.keys() to iterate through fields. Export the class as default.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JSDoc with @typedef for ValidationRule object (with optional required, minLength, maxLength, pattern, custom properties), @typedef for ValidationRules (object mapping field names to ValidationRule), @typedef for ValidationErrors (object mapping field names to strings or string arrays), @class, @param, and @returns. Export the class.

variants.typescript: Write a TypeScript FormValidator class that validates form data against rules. Include interfaces for validation rules and results.
variants.javascript: Write a JavaScript FormValidator class that validates form data against rules.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Write a JavaScript FormValidator class with JSDoc that validates form data against rules.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web:
Create a registration form with client-side validation in vanilla JavaScript. Include:

**Form Fields:**
- Username (required, 3-20 chars, alphanumeric)
- Email (required, valid email format)
- Password (required, min 8 chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number)
- Confirm Password (required, must match password)
- Age (required, 18-120)
- Terms checkbox (required)

**Validation:**
- Real-time validation on blur
- Show error messages below each field
- Disable submit button until form is valid
- Show all errors on submit attempt
- Visual indicators (red border for errors, green for valid)

**HTML:**
- Semantic form structure
- Label for each input
- Error message containers
- Submit button

**CSS:**
- Clean form design
- Error styling (red)
- Success styling (green)
- Focus states

**JavaScript:**
- Validation functions for each field type
- Real-time validation handlers
- Form submission handler
- Display/clear error messages

Return as single HTML file with working validation.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web-jsdoc:
Same as javascript-vanilla-web, plus complete JSDoc:

- @typedef for ValidationRule
- @typedef for ValidationResult
- @typedef for FormField
- Document all validation functions
- @param and @return for all functions

Return as single HTML file.
variants.typescript-vanilla-web:
Create a form validation system using TypeScript and vanilla Web APIs. Include:

**TypeScript:**
- Interface for ValidationRule<T>
- Interface for FieldConfig
- Type-safe validator functions
- Generic FormValidator<T> class
- Proper typing for form data

**Validation Rules:**
- Required
- MinLength/MaxLength
- Pattern (regex)
- Custom validators
- Async validators (e.g., check username availability)

**Features:**
- Real-time validation
- Field-level and form-level validation
- Error message handling
- Type-safe form data

Provide TypeScript source and HTML structure.
variants.typescript-react:
Create a form with validation using TypeScript React. Include:

**Components:**
- Form (main container)
- FormField (reusable field with validation)
- FormError (error display)

**Custom Hook:**
- useForm<T> hook with TypeScript
- Generic form state management
- Validation logic
- Submit handling

**TypeScript:**
- Interface for form data
- Type-safe validation rules
- Proper hook typing
- Generic FormField component

**Features:**
- Real-time validation
- Touched/dirty state tracking
- Custom validation rules
- Async validation support
- TypeScript strict mode

**Example:**
```tsx
interface FormData {
  username: string;
  email: string;
  password: string;
}

const { values, errors, handleChange, handleSubmit } = useForm<FormData>({
  initialValues: { username: '', email: '', password: '' },
  validationRules: { ... }
});
```

No form libraries (e.g., no Formik, react-hook-form). Build from scratch.

performanceBenchmarks.name: validate-email-formats
performanceBenchmarks.code: const emailRegex = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/; const emails = Array.from({length: 100}, (_, i) => `test${i}@example.com`); for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) { emails.forEach(email => emailRegex.test(email)); }

performanceBenchmarks.name: validate-form-fields
performanceBenchmarks.code: const validateField = (value, required, minLength) => { if (required && !value) return false; if (minLength && value.length < minLength) return false; return true; }; for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) { validateField("test", true, 3); validateField("", false, 0); validateField("ab", true, 3); }
